preview: In this episode, we look at how cafés are responding to people who work on laptops. The issue is how to make room for work while also serving people who come for coffee, conversation, and shorter visits. This matters because a café’s rules and design can shape the kind of place it becomes. By the end, you will understand the choices cafés are considering and the question behind them: what should a café be for?
comment_1: Listen for the four types of café described in the study.
comment_2: So far, we have seen that cafés are trying different ways to deal with people who work there. In Part 2, what choice did one café make when laptop users stayed for a long time?
comment_3: This story shows that cafés are making different choices about people who work there. Some try to serve both workers and social customers, while others set limits. Next, we will look at two more ways to understand these choices.
comment_4: So far, we have seen that a café’s design can guide how people use the space. We have also seen that customers who work there may offer the café more than their payment. Now, let’s connect these ideas in the closing summary.
